posts.hook: Simba promised the best dinner in the city.

slides.title: Episode 1: The Worst Chef
slides.body: Simba promised the city's best dinner. Nico had already polished the cutlery. Twice.

slides.title: Then the kitchen happened
slides.body: A dropped pan, a flare of garlic and one very fast Milo. The plate went straight to the city's most feared critic.

slides.title: The critic asked for more
slides.body: Nobody understood why. Luna noticed something folded under the plate: the first clue to the missing recipe book.

slides.title: The dish is real
slides.body: Creamy Tomato Dreams. 25 minutes, serves 2, and you can cook it tonight.

posts.cta: Who do you suspect? Recipe at the link in bio.
posts.caption:
Episode 1 of The Lost Recipe Book.

Simba promised the city's best dinner. What arrived at the critic's table was… memorable. And then the critic asked for another plate.

Luna thinks it's a clue. Milo thinks it's dinner.

The dish from tonight's episode is real: Creamy Tomato Dreams, 25 minutes, serves 2. The full recipe is at the link in bio.

Who do you suspect took the book? Tell us below.
posts.alt_text: Simba the ginger cat chef and Nico the tuxedo cat in a warm kitchen, with the title Simba promised the best dinner in the city.
hook_alternates: The worst chef in the city. Or is he?
One dinner. One critic. One missing recipe book.
Simba said it was exactly what he meant to do.

posts.hook: The dish from Episode 1, for real: Creamy Tomato Dreams.

slides.title: 25 minutes, serves 2
slides.body: Silky tomato sauce softened with cream, tossed through pasta with Parmesan and torn basil.

slides.title: What you need
slides.body: 180 g pasta, 400 g chopped tomatoes, 2 garlic cloves, 60 ml double cream, 25 g Parmesan, basil, olive oil.

slides.title: How it comes together
slides.body: Garlic in warm oil for 1 minute. Tomatoes for 10. Cream, pasta and a splash of pasta water. Parmesan and basil off the heat.

slides.title: Simba's version
slides.body: He added the basil with his whole paw. Yours can be a little more careful.

posts.cta: Save it for tonight. Full recipe at the link in bio.
posts.caption:
The dish that sent a food critic back for seconds in Episode 1.

Creamy Tomato Dreams: silky tomato sauce, a little cream, Parmesan and torn basil. 25 minutes, serves 2.

Save this for tonight, and find the full recipe with quantities and every step at the link in bio. Allergens: wheat, milk. Always check your labels.
posts.alt_text: A bowl of creamy tomato pasta with Parmesan and basil on a rustic table.
hook_alternates: The pasta a critic asked for twice.
25 minutes. One pan of sauce. Dinner sorted.
Episode 1's dish, step by step.

posts.hook: Nico runs a perfect shift. Milo is just checking the pastries.

slides.title: Naughty Cat Café
slides.body: “We can resolve this with dignity.” — Nico. “I was just checking…” — Milo, mouth full.

posts.cta: Who would you hire? Tell us below.
posts.caption:
Every café needs a Nico: calm, polite, impossibly organised.

Every café also seems to get a Milo.

The pastries were counted at opening. The count has changed. Milo says he was just checking.

Who would you hire for the morning shift?
posts.alt_text: Nico the tuxedo cat holding a folded napkin beside Milo the cream cat holding a pastry.
hook_alternates: The pastry count has changed. Again.
Perfect service. Imperfect colleague.
Nico has a plan. Milo has a croissant.

posts.hook: Crispy chickpeas, cool cucumber, lemon yogurt. 35 minutes.

slides.title: Crispy Chickpea & Couscous Bowls
slides.body: Spiced roasted chickpeas over couscous with cucumber, tomatoes and a lemon yogurt dressing. Serves 2.

slides.title: The trick for real crunch
slides.body: Dry the rinsed chickpeas well before they go in the oven. Roast 25–30 minutes, shaking halfway.

slides.title: Build the bowl
slides.body: Couscous first, then cucumber and tomatoes, hot chickpeas, lemon yogurt and parsley. Eat straight away for the crunch.

posts.cta: Save it for a weeknight. Recipe at the link in bio.
posts.caption:
A simple, balanced bowl for a weeknight.

Smoked paprika and cumin chickpeas, roasted until crisp, over fluffy couscous with cucumber, cherry tomatoes and a quick lemon yogurt.

The one trick: dry the chickpeas properly before they roast.

Full recipe at the link in bio. Allergens: wheat, milk. Check your labels.
posts.alt_text: Two bowls of couscous topped with crispy chickpeas, cucumber, tomatoes and yogurt.
hook_alternates: The chickpea trick for real crunch.
A weeknight bowl in 35 minutes.
Crunchy, fresh and on the table tonight.

posts.hook: One tray of tomatoes, one can of beans, soup for four.

slides.title: Roasted Tomato & White Bean Soup
slides.body: Oven-roasted tomatoes, onion and garlic blended with cannellini beans. Serves 4.

slides.title: The tray does the work
slides.body: Tomatoes, onion and garlic with oil, salt and pepper. 30–35 minutes at 200°C, stir once.

slides.title: Everyday ingredients
slides.body: Tomatoes, an onion, garlic, a can of beans and stock. Nothing fancy, and very little left over.

posts.cta: Save it for soup night. Recipe at the link in bio.
posts.caption:
Budget Cat, week one.

One tray of roasted tomatoes, onion and garlic, a can of cannellini beans and some stock. Blend, and that's soup for four.

Everyday ingredients, very little waste, and Milo insists on testing every spoonful.

Full recipe at the link in bio.
posts.alt_text: A bowl of roasted tomato soup with basil and olive oil beside crusty bread.
hook_alternates: Soup for four from one tray.
Everyday ingredients, a very good soup.
Roast, blend, done.

posts.hook: Sunday, slowly: warm apple and oat crumble.

slides.title: Warm Apple & Oat Crumble
slides.body: Cinnamon apples under a buttery oat crumble, baked until the juices bubble. Let it stand 10 minutes; the fruit is very hot.

posts.cta: Save it for a slow Sunday. Recipe at the link in bio.
posts.caption:
A slow one for Sunday.

Apples tossed with cinnamon and a little sugar, a crumble rubbed together by hand, and 35–40 minutes in the oven while the kitchen fills with the smell of it.

Let it stand for 10 minutes before serving; the fruit will be very hot.

Full recipe at the link in bio. Allergens: wheat, oats, milk.

Apples, oats, butter, patience.
A crumble for a quiet afternoon.
